# Student Churn exercise (Exercise 1, Week 8)

Source: StudentChurn.pdf, 2 pages, no author/date visible. Work in groups of 2-3. (Data schema: StudentChurn_csv.md)

**What is churn rate?** The rate at which customers stop doing business with an entity; most commonly the percentage of subscribers who discontinue within a given period (also the rate at which employees leave jobs). For a company to expand, its growth rate (new customers) must exceed its churn rate.

**Churn in higher education in Denmark.** The data is fictive, generated by a Python program, but distributions are based on actual churn rates. Churn is a problem for the student (stops before a diploma) and the institution. Predicting churn well in advance would allow preventive action: counselling, assignment to study groups, allocation of homework-support resources.

Task as data scientist: is it possible to predict whether a student will complete an education or not, from the available data?

The dataset (studentchurn) is on Canvas as .csv. A file "studentchurn.py" for reading it into a pandas dataframe is also on Canvas. Data contains an id per student, line for previously completed education, grade average, distance from home to school, and study group membership (if available).

## A) Getting to know the data and the problem
What kind of ML problem is this? Be as precise as possible. How many different features (not counting labels) are in the dataset? How many of these would the Y-data (labels) consist of?

## B) Cleaning the data
Decide which features to use for the X training set, and what to do with missing data for the features you keep. Some data is non-numerical and must be converted to numbers (in both training and test set). Easy with pandas, e.g. `xtrain['Sex'] = xtrain['Sex'].replace(['female'],1.0 )` (male would also need a value).

After cleaning (and scaling; see slides and earlier exercises), split into two sets: one for training and one for evaluating performance. How many rows in training vs test? Give reasons.

## C) Choosing a model, training, evaluating on the test set
Choose a model and explain why. Train it. Evaluate performance. Can you predict churn yes/no? How well?
